/bls/productivity/tables.description: Fetch a BLS Productivity prod2 supplemental table in long form (every column preserved).
/bls/productivity/tables.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Quarterly Nonfarm business sector labor productivity (the default headline series).
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls')
# Manufacturing sector unit labor costs, quarterly.
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls', sector='Manufacturing sector', measure='Unit labor costs')
# Total economy hours worked, in billions of hours.
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls', dataset='total-economy-hours-employment', sector='Total economy', measure='Hours worked', units='Billions of hours')
# Nonfarm business labor productivity growth by business cycle.
obb.bls.productivity.tables(provider='bls', dataset='major-sectors-business-cycles', units='Compound annual growth rate')
```

options.label: major-sectors-quarterly — Quarterly labor productivity and related measures, major sectors.
major-sectors-annual — Annual labor productivity and related measures, major sectors.
major-sectors-business-cycles — Labor productivity major sectors, compound annual growth rates by approximate business cycle period.
total-economy-hours-employment — Quarterly hours worked and employment, total U.S. economy and subsectors.

bls.name: start_date
bls.description: Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

bls.name: end_date
bls.description: End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

bls.name: sector
bls.description: Sector to restrict the results. Defaults to the headline Nonfarm business sector; clear it to load every sector.

bls.name: measure
bls.description: Measure to restrict the results. Defaults to Labor productivity; clear it to load every measure.

bls.name: units
bls.description: Units to restrict the results. Defaults to the 2017=100 index (one row per period); clear it to load every units basis. The source is long-form, so leaving every dimension open returns one row per sector / measure / units / period.

options.label: Hours worked per job per week
options.value: Hours worked per job per week

bls.name: date
bls.description: First-of-period date the observation applies to.

bls.name: period_kind
bls.description: Period kind for the row (quarter, annual, or business cycle).

bls.name: year
bls.description: Year reported in the source XLSX.

bls.name: quarter
bls.description: Quarter index reported in the source XLSX.

bls.name: sector
bls.description: BLS sector this row belongs to.

bls.name: basis
bls.description: Worker-counting basis used for the row.

bls.name: component
bls.description: Sub-sector component for the total-economy workbook.

bls.name: units
bls.description: Units the value is expressed in.

bls.name: value_string
bls.description: Raw cell text when the value isn't numeric.

bls.description: Business-cycle period label as published by BLS.

bls.name: cycle_start_date
bls.description: First-of-quarter start date for the business-cycle period.

bls.name: cycle_end_date
bls.description: First-of-quarter end date for the business-cycle period.

bls.name: row_index
bls.description: Sequential parser order preserving the source layout.

bls.name: source_file
bls.description: Filename of the source XLSX on bls.gov.

bls.description: Release date stamped in the workbook header.

/bls/search.description: Search the BLS series catalog by category, keyword, or code.
/bls/search.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Search the CPI category for series matching a query.
obb.bls.search(provider='bls', category='cpi', query='urban')
# List every series in the JOLTS category.
obb.bls.search(provider='bls', category='jolts')
```

standard.name: query
standard.description: The search word(s). Use semi-colon to separate multiple queries as an & operator.

bls.name: symbol
bls.description: Bound to the Series widget via cell-click grouping; clicking a row's symbol loads it there. Does not filter the search results. Multiple items allowed.

bls.name: category
bls.description:
The category of BLS survey to search within. An empty search query returns every series within the category. Options are:

    cpi - Consumer Price Index
    ixp - Import/Export Price Indexes
    pce - Consumer Expenditure Survey
    ppi - Producer Price Index
    ip - Productivity (Industry, Major Sector & Total Factor)
    jolts - Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey
    nfp - Nonfarm Payrolls (Current Employment Statistics)
    cps - Current Population Survey
    lfs - Labor Force Statistics & International Comparisons
    wages - Employment Cost Index & Wage Estimates
    ec - Employer Costs for Employee Compensation
    sla - State & Local Area Employment & Unemployment
    bed - Business Employment Dynamics
    tu - American Time Use Survey

options.label: Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey

bls.name: include_extras
bls.description: Include additional information in the search results. Extra fields returned are metadata and vary by survey. Fields are undefined strings that typically have names ending with '_code'.

bls.name: include_code_map
bls.description: When True, includes the complete code map for eaçh survey in the category, returned separately as a nested JSON to the `extras['results_metadata']` property of the response. Example content is the NAICS industry map for PPI surveys. Each code is a value within the 'symbol' of the time series.

standard.name: symbol
standard.description: Symbol representing the entity requested in the data.

standard.name: title
standard.description: The title of the series.

standard.name: survey_name
standard.description: The name of the survey.

bls.name: symbol
bls.description: BLS series identifier. Click a cell to load it into the linked BLS Series widget.

/cftc/swap_trades.description: Get swap transaction and pricing data disseminated by DTCC.
/cftc/swap_trades.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.swap_trades(provider='cftc')
# Get USD SOFR swap transactions reported on a given date.
obb.cftc.swap_trades(asset_class='rates', currency='USD', underlier='SOFR', action_type='NEWT', provider='cftc')
# Get large cleared credit transactions.
obb.cftc.swap_trades(asset_class='credits', cleared='Y', min_notional=50000000, provider='cftc')
```

cftc.name: asset_class
cftc.description: Asset class of the transactions. Only the two priceable classes are offered: rates, valued against the DTCC-reported curve, and forex. Credit index prints have their own CDS Index Trades endpoint.

cftc.name: start_date
cftc.description: Start of the report-date window (UTC). Default is the end date, a single day. Every day in the window is a separately published file, so a long window is a proportionally larger download.

cftc.name: end_date
cftc.description: End of the report-date window (UTC). Default is the most recent date whose file holds transactions matching the query; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Retained 366 days.

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Filter by the leg 1 notional currency. E.g., 'USD'.

cftc.name: underlier
cftc.description: Filter by UPI underlier name, matched as a case-insensitive substring. E.g., 'SOFR'.

cftc.name: upi_fisn
cftc.description: Filter by UPI FISN, matched as a case-insensitive substring. E.g., 'Swap OIS'.

cftc.name: ticker
cftc.description: Filter to the exact UPI ticker, the Unique Product Identifier the source's TICKER report keys on. E.g., 'QZXQ4R16245X' for a SOFR OIS. The window is answered by the source's search API, one filtered query across the date range, cached per day.

cftc.name: action_type
cftc.description: Filter by action type. E.g., 'NEWT' for new trades.

cftc.name: cleared
cftc.description: Filter by whether the transaction is centrally cleared. True keeps cleared and intent-to-clear trades (Cleared 'Y' or 'I'); False keeps bilateral trades (Cleared 'N').

cftc.name: trade_type
cftc.description: Filter by trade-type family, for the rates asset class: 'spot' and 'forward' are single-currency fixed-vs-floating swaps in a recognized curve family, split by whether the trade has already started; 'basis' floats two indices in the same currency against each other; 'cross_currency' floats two different currencies; 'inflation' is a zero-coupon swap of a fixed breakeven against a published price index. Ignored outside the rates asset class.

/cftc/swap_valuation.description: Value a disseminated swap on its own printed terms against the rate curve.
/cftc/swap_valuation.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.swap_valuation(provider='cftc')
# Value a specific disseminated print against today's curve.
obb.cftc.swap_valuation(currency='USD', dissemination_identifier='4339565190000000401', provider='cftc')
# Value the largest CNY print off its fixed-float IRS curve.
obb.cftc.swap_valuation(currency='CNY', provider='cftc')
```

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the swap, priced off that currency's reported rate curve - its OIS, or its fixed-vs-floating IRS when it has no OIS (CNY, TWD, MYR, ...).

cftc.name: dissemination_identifier
cftc.description: The disseminated trade to value, as printed on the Swap Transactions tape. Any non-matured print is valuable by its own identifier. Default is the day's largest standalone par print; a package leg or off-par print's rate may reflect a package structure rather than a market level, flagged `is_vanilla_par` in the metadata rather than excluded.

cftc.name: trade_date
cftc.description: Dissemination date the trade printed on (UTC). Default is the curve date, today's tape; an older print is looked up on the day it was disseminated and valued on its remaining life against the current curve. Slices are retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: side
cftc.description: Whether the position pays or receives the fixed rate. The net present value is signed to this side; dissemination does not say which side either counterparty took.

cftc.name: min_notional
cftc.description: Only consider prints at least this large when defaulting to the day's largest. Ignored when a dissemination identifier is given.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC) of the trades and the rate curve. Default is the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: min_trades
cftc.description: Minimum trades for a curve node. The default keeps every traded tenor, because thin EM curves would otherwise lose their pillars.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

cftc.name: period
cftc.description: Coupon period, ordered from the first payment to maturity.

cftc.name: start_date
cftc.description: Start of the accrual period.

cftc.name: payment_date
cftc.description: Payment date at the end of the accrual period.

cftc.name: year_fraction
cftc.description: Accrual year fraction of the period, on the currency's money-market day count.

cftc.name: discount_factor
cftc.description: Discount factor to the payment date, off the bootstrapped curve.

cftc.name: forward_rate
cftc.description: Curve-implied forward rate for the period, in percent. Reported on the fixed leg's rows where the floating leg's periods align with them.

cftc.name: floating_rate
cftc.description: Floating rate applied to the period, in percent - the curve's implied forward plus the contract spread.

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the swap, priced off that currency's reported rate curve - its OIS, or its fixed-vs-floating IRS when it has no OIS (CNY, TWD, MYR, ...).

cftc.name: dissemination_identifier
cftc.description: The disseminated trade to value, as printed on the Swap Transactions tape. Any non-matured print is valuable by its own identifier. Default is the day's largest standalone par print; a package leg or off-par print's rate may reflect a package structure rather than a market level, flagged `is_vanilla_par` in the metadata rather than excluded.

cftc.name: trade_date
cftc.description: Dissemination date the trade printed on (UTC). Default is the curve date, today's tape; an older print is looked up on the day it was disseminated and valued on its remaining life against the current curve. Slices are retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: side
cftc.description: Whether the position pays or receives the fixed rate. The net present value is signed to this side; dissemination does not say which side either counterparty took.

cftc.name: min_notional
cftc.description: Only consider prints at least this large when defaulting to the day's largest. Ignored when a dissemination identifier is given.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC) of the trades and the rate curve. Default is the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: min_trades
cftc.description: Minimum trades for a curve node. The default keeps every traded tenor, because thin EM curves would otherwise lose their pillars.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

cftc.name: metric
cftc.description: Name of the summary metric.

cftc.name: value
cftc.description: Value of the summary metric, formatted in its own unit.

cftc.name: detail
cftc.description: Context the metric carries beyond its value.

/cftc/cds_index_trades.description: Get credit default swap index transactions disseminated by DTCC.
/cftc/cds_index_trades.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.cds_index_trades(provider='cftc')
# Get the CDX.NA.IG tape.
obb.cftc.cds_index_trades(index='CDX.NA.IG', provider='cftc')
# Get the 5Y CDX.NA.HY prints of at least 10mm notional.
obb.cftc.cds_index_trades(index='CDX.NA.HY', tenor='5Y', min_notional=10000000, provider='cftc')
```

cftc.name: index
cftc.description: Filter by index family, matched against the UPI Underlier Name. E.g., 'CDX.NA.IG'. Matching is exact and case-insensitive, because 'ITRAXX EUROPE' is a substring of two other index families. Default is every index.

options.label: IBOXX USD LIQUID LEVERAGED LOANS INDEX
options.value: IBOXX USD LIQUID LEVERAGED LOANS INDEX

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC). Default is the most recent date whose file holds index prints matching the query; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Files are retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: tenor
cftc.description: Filter by the print's tenor at execution. E.g., '5Y'. Default is every tenor.

cftc.name: min_notional
cftc.description: Filter out prints whose leg 1 notional is disseminated below this amount. A print above the reporting cap is disseminated at the cap, which is only a floor on its true size, so a threshold above a cap drops prints that may in fact exceed it. Caps vary by index, tenor and currency.

cftc.name: limit
cftc.description: Number of prints to return. Default is all matching.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

cftc.name: dissemination_date
cftc.description: Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in. The cumulative file carries no per-message dissemination timestamp.

cftc.name: trade_key
cftc.description: Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'CR:4411567497000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

cftc.name: action_type
cftc.description: Type of action taken on the swap transaction: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), EROR (error), TERM (terminate), or REVI (revive).

cftc.name: event_type
cftc.description: Explanation or reason for the action being taken on the swap transaction: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation/step-in), COMP (compression or post trade risk reduction exercise), ETRM (early termination), CLRG (clearing), EXER (exercise), or CREV (credit event).

cftc.name: event_timestamp
cftc.description: Date and time of occurrence of the event, as determined by the reporting counterparty or a service provider.

cftc.name: execution_timestamp
cftc.description: Date and time the transaction was originally executed, resulting in the generation of a new UTI. It remains unchanged throughout the life of the UTI, so on a correction or termination it dates the original trade.

cftc.name: index
cftc.description: Name of the asset or index underlying the product corresponding to the UPI. It names the index family only and carries no series number, so `maturity_date` is what pins the series.

cftc.name: upi_fisn
cftc.description: ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name issued by the UPI Service Provider. 'NA/CDS Corp Idx Tra' marks a tranche print.

cftc.name: unique_product_identifier
cftc.description: ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier (UPI), a unique set of characters that represents a particular OTC derivative.

cftc.name: effective_date
cftc.description: Unadjusted date at which obligations under the transaction come into effect. For a credit index this should be the effective date of the contract, usually one or two days after execution, and not the roll date of the underlying index.

cftc.name: maturity_date
cftc.description: Unadjusted date at which obligations under the transaction stop being effective, as included in the confirmation ('Expiration date'). Early termination does not affect it. Together with `index` it identifies the series traded.

cftc.name: tenor
cftc.description: Years from `execution_timestamp` to `maturity_date`, snapped to the nearest standard CDS index tenor within one year, else the rounded year count. Derived, not disseminated.

cftc.name: coupon
cftc.description: Per annum rate of the fixed leg, expressed as a decimal (0.05 is 500bp). The index's standardised coupon, and with `upfront_amount` the price of the print.

cftc.name: coupon_day_count
cftc.description: ISO 20022 day count convention of the fixed leg. A004 is ACT/360.

cftc.name: coupon_payment_frequency
cftc.description: Time unit associated with the frequency of fixed leg payments: DAIL, WEEK, MNTH, YEAR, ADHO, or EXPI (payment at term).

cftc.name: coupon_payment_frequency_multiplier
cftc.description: Number of time units of `coupon_payment_frequency` between payments. MNTH with a multiplier of 3 is quarterly.

cftc.name: upfront_amount
cftc.description: Payment amount corresponding to `upfront_type`, in `upfront_currency`. With `coupon` it prices the print.

cftc.name: upfront_type
cftc.description: Type of the other payment amount. UFRO is an upfront payment: the initial payment made by one of the counterparties either to bring a transaction to fair value or for any other reason that may be the cause of an off-market transaction. UWIN is an unwind or full termination payment; PEXH is a principal exchange.

cftc.name: upfront_currency
cftc.description: Currency in which `upfront_amount` is denominated.

cftc.name: spread
cftc.description: Reported spread on the leg 1 index reference price, as disseminated. Conditional: it is required only where `coupon` is not populated and `upfront_type` is not 'UFRO', so it is an alternative to the coupon-plus-upfront quote rather than the price of the print. Read it together with `spread_notation` - the field also carries a price in points of par on the price-quoted indices. See the package README.

cftc.name: spread_notation
cftc.description: Manner in which `spread` is expressed: 1 (monetary amount, in `spread_currency`), 3 (decimal, e.g. 0.0257 for 2.57%), or 4 (basis points, e.g. 257 for 2.57%).

cftc.name: spread_currency
cftc.description: Currency in which `spread` is denominated. Only applicable when `spread_notation` is 1.

cftc.name: index_factor
cftc.description: The index version factor or percent, expressed as a decimal value, that multiplied by the notional amount yields the notional amount covered by the seller of protection. Below 1 once a constituent has defaulted.

cftc.name: notional_amount
cftc.description: Leg 1 notional amount specified in the contract, gross of any version incrementing due to a credit event. Values above the reporting cap are disseminated at the cap and flagged by `is_capped`.

cftc.name: notional_currency
cftc.description: Currency in which the leg 1 notional amount is denominated.

cftc.name: is_capped
cftc.description: Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap rather than its true value. Other disseminated amounts are proportionally scaled when the notional is capped.

cftc.name: venue
cftc.description: ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility the transaction was executed on. XOFF marks a transaction in a listed instrument executed off venue, XXXX an instrument not listed on any venue, and BILT a reporting counterparty that could not determine whether the instrument is listed.

cftc.name: cleared
cftc.description: Whether the transaction has been cleared, or is intended to be cleared, by a central counterparty: Y (centrally cleared), N (not centrally cleared), or I (intent to clear, for original swaps planned to be submitted to clearing).

cftc.name: block_trade
cftc.description: Whether an election has been made to report the transaction as a block trade, by the reporting counterparty or as calculated by the SDR on its behalf or by a third party.

cftc.name: package_trade
cftc.description: Whether the transaction is part of a package transaction, being two or more transactions negotiated together as the product of a single economic agreement.

widget_config.name: CDS Index Trades
widget_config.description: DTCC Public Price Dissemination credit default swap index transactions.

/cftc/ois_curve.description: Get an overnight index swap curve, built from executed swap transactions.
/cftc/ois_curve.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get the USD SOFR curve.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(provider='cftc')
# Get the EUR ESTR curve.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(currency='EUR', provider='cftc')
# Fill in a thinly traded currency's short end, which needs a longer window and admits single prints.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(currency='CHF', lookback_days=30, min_trades=1, provider='cftc')
# Get the curve at every distinct tenor traded, not just benchmarks.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(granularity='observed', min_trades=1, provider='cftc')
# Build from a single day's file instead of a search window.
obb.cftc.ois_curve(source='slice', provider='cftc')
```

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the swap curve. Each maps to that currency's overnight benchmark rate. Currencies whose overnight index swaps are too thinly reported to bootstrap a curve are not offered. CNY builds from FR007 fixed-float swaps, backstopped by the CFETS daily bulletin's traded curve.

cftc.name: curve_type
cftc.description: Which representation of the curve to return in `rate`: the par swap rate or the annually compounded zero rate. The forward curve is a separate endpoint, `ois_forward_curve`.

cftc.name: source
cftc.description: Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days and prices each tenor from the most recent day it traded in depth. 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, walking a weekend or holiday back to the most recent day that priced this currency, which still leaves sparse tenors missing.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC). With source='search' this ends the lookback window, and defaults to today. With source='slice' it selects the most recent day on or before it that priced this currency, defaulting to the latest. History is retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: lookback_days
cftc.description: Number of dissemination days to look back over, ending on `date`. With source='search' a longer window fills in more tenors, at the cost of pricing the thin ones further from today; check `staleness_days` and cap it with `max_staleness_days`. A thinly traded currency reaches a full curve only over a long window - the search chains 180-day sub-windows up to the one-year horizon. With source='slice' it is how far back to walk for the most recent day that priced this currency.

cftc.name: max_staleness_days
cftc.description: Drop any node whose freshest print is older than this many days, measured from the curve's own date. A wide `lookback_days` fills thin tenors but resurrects some that last traded months ago in a different rate regime; capping staleness keeps the curve current rather than a mosaic of old levels. Only meaningful with source='search'. None keeps every live node and reports its age in `staleness_days`. Nodes that have already matured by the curve date are always dropped, cap or none.

cftc.name: granularity
cftc.description: Tenor axis of the curve. 'benchmark' snaps trades to standard nodes; 'observed' emits a node for every distinct tenor traded, including broken dates.

cftc.name: aggregation
cftc.description: How each node's executed rates are reduced to a par rate. Median is the default because notionals above the reporting cap are disseminated at the cap, which biases notional-weighted averages.

cftc.name: min_trades
cftc.description: Drop nodes priced by fewer than this many trades on their as-of day. The default keeps every node, because one executed trade is still a price; `num_trades`, `min_rate` and `max_rate` say how thin it is. Raise it to admit only nodes several trades agree on, at the cost of losing the tenors a thin currency never trades in depth on any single day.

cftc.name: cleared
cftc.description: Keep only centrally cleared or intent-to-clear trades, dropping the bilateral uncleared prints that carry most of the off-market noise. Most useful with granularity='observed', where thin nodes are exposed to it.

cftc.name: interpolation
cftc.description: How discount factors are interpolated between pillars, on the log of the discount factor. 'log_linear' is piecewise linear, giving piecewise-flat instantaneous forwards. 'log_cubic' is a monotone Hermite cubic, giving smooth forwards without overshooting into negative rates.

cftc.name: overnight_anchor
cftc.description: Anchor the curve's front end with the benchmark's latest published overnight fixing, as a 1-day node. The fixing is a realized rate, so the node carries no trades and its own as-of date.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the source data locally. Closed dissemination days are immutable and are never re-fetched; daily files are revalidated against the source ETag.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Date of the curve, being that of its freshest node.

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the curve.

cftc.name: benchmark
cftc.description: Overnight benchmark rate the swaps reference (SOFR, ESTR, ...).

cftc.name: index
cftc.description: Curve index plotted on the chart and used as the row index: the tenor label under 'benchmark' granularity, else the node's maturity date under 'observed' granularity.

cftc.name: as_of_date
cftc.description: Dissemination date the node's trades were reported on. Nodes are priced from the most recent day that cleared min_trades, so a thin tenor is dated earlier than a deep one.

cftc.name: staleness_days
cftc.description: Days between the node's as-of date and the curve's date. Zero on the freshest nodes.

cftc.name: tenor
cftc.description: Tenor of the curve node.

cftc.name: tenor_days
cftc.description: Tenor of the node, in days.

cftc.name: tenor_years
cftc.description: Tenor of the node, in years, on an ACT/365F basis.

cftc.name: maturity_date
cftc.description: Maturity date implied by the node's tenor, from its as-of date. Under 'observed' granularity this is also the curve's index.

cftc.name: rate
cftc.description: Rate of the selected `curve_type` at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%): the par swap rate or the annually compounded zero rate. In percent rather than a decimal so the chart axis reads as a rate - the grid formatter is not applied to the chart. Omitted where the bootstrap degenerates.

cftc.name: curve_type
cftc.description: Which representation `rate` holds: par or zero.

cftc.name: discount_factor
cftc.description: Discount factor bootstrapped to the node's maturity.

cftc.name: day_count
cftc.description: Fixed-leg day count convention the node's trades reported, used to accrue the fixed leg in the bootstrap. ACT/360 for USD, EUR, CHF, MXN, COP and CLP; ACT/365F for GBP, JPY, CAD, SGD, INR, ZAR, THB, ILS, AUD and NZD. BRL reports BUS/252, recovered to the same year fraction on calendar days.

cftc.name: num_trades
cftc.description: Number of executed trades aggregated into the node.

cftc.name: total_notional
cftc.description: Sum of the leg 1 notional of the node's trades.

cftc.name: min_rate
cftc.description: Lowest executed rate at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

cftc.name: max_rate
cftc.description: Highest executed rate at the node, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

cftc.name: is_capped
cftc.description: Whether any trade at the node had its notional disseminated at the reporting cap.

widget_config.name: Overnight Index Swap Curve
widget_config.description: Central bank overnight index swap curves built from executed transactions.

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the swap curve.

cftc.name: forward_tenor
cftc.description: Length of the forward swap - the tenor of the swap priced at each forward start date. Independent of the spacing between starts.

cftc.name: forward_step
cftc.description: Spacing between forward start dates. Set it apart from `forward_tenor` to plot, say, the 5Y forward at yearly starts (forward_tenor='5Y', forward_step='1Y').

cftc.name: forward_count
cftc.description: Number of forward start dates to plot. Defaults to the whole curve out to its last pillar; set it to plot only the first N steps (e.g. 10 with a 1Y step is the next ten years of the forward).

cftc.name: method
cftc.description: How the forward rates are formed. 'implied' reads them off the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson fit of the bootstrapped spot curve. 'observed' takes the fixed rates of the forward-starting swaps of the tenor directly, medianed by start and smoothed onto the grid - the market's own forward quotes, which reach only as far as that forward has traded.

cftc.name: source
cftc.description: Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days; 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, walking a weekend or holiday back to the most recent day that priced this currency.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC). Ends the search window, or selects the most recent slice on or before it that priced this currency. History is retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: lookback_days
cftc.description: Days to look back over: the search window with source='search', or how far to walk back for the most recent priced day with source='slice'. The search chains 180-day sub-windows up to the one-year horizon, so a thin currency can fill its forwards from a full year of prints.

cftc.name: max_staleness_days
cftc.description: Drop any underlying node whose freshest print is older than this many days. A wide `lookback_days` fills thin tenors but resurrects some that last traded months ago; capping staleness keeps the forward strip current. Only meaningful with source='search'.

cftc.name: aggregation
cftc.description: How each node's executed rates are reduced to a par rate.

cftc.name: min_trades
cftc.description: Drop nodes priced by fewer than this many trades.

cftc.name: interpolation
cftc.description: Discount-factor interpolation for the bootstrap the Nelson-Siegel-Svensson forward fit is drawn from.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Date of the curve.

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the curve.

cftc.name: index
cftc.description: Forward start date of the swap - the row and chart index.

cftc.name: tenor
cftc.description: The forward swap and its start, e.g. '1Y @ 5.00Y' (a 1Y swap 5Y out).

cftc.name: start_years
cftc.description: Forward start of the swap, in years. 0 is spot.

cftc.name: forward_rate
cftc.description: Forward par swap rate, in percent (4.32 is 4.32%).

cftc.name: extrapolated
cftc.description: Whether the swap's tail ran past the last pillar, extended by the fit.

cftc.name: num_trades
cftc.description: Trades behind the curve nodes spanning this forward's start-to-tenor span, or the nearest node's when none fall inside it.

widget_config.name: OIS Forward Rate Curve
widget_config.description: Forward par swap rate by start date, from executed transactions.

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the policy path, read from its forward-starting OIS. Only the currencies whose central banks trade meeting-dated OIS in depth are offered.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC) the path is built as of; defaults to the most recent. It anchors the forward start, so a window ending here is used and a trade whose start has since rolled to spot drops out.

cftc.name: lookback_days
cftc.description: Number of recent daily files to combine, ending on `date`. Meeting-dated OIS are thin on any single day, so a handful of files are pooled to price each forward start in depth; a node's own freshest day is reported as `as_of_date`.

cftc.name: min_trades
cftc.description: Drop a forward start priced by fewer than this many trades across the window. The default trims the one-off prints that are not meeting nodes.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the source data locally, revalidating against the source ETag.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Date the path is built as of.

cftc.name: currency
cftc.description: Currency of the path.

cftc.name: index
cftc.description: Forward start date of the period - the row and chart index.

cftc.name: rate
cftc.description: Expected average overnight rate over the period, in percent.

cftc.name: forward_days
cftc.description: Days from the curve date to the period's start.

cftc.name: start_date
cftc.description: Start (effective date) of the period.

cftc.name: end_date
cftc.description: End (maturity) of the period.

cftc.name: tenor_days
cftc.description: Length of the period, in days.

cftc.name: num_trades
cftc.description: Trades pricing the node across the window.

cftc.name: as_of_date
cftc.description: Freshest day the node's trades were disseminated on.

cftc.name: staleness_days
cftc.description: Days between the node's as-of day and the path's freshest node.

cftc.name: min_rate
cftc.description: Lowest executed rate at the node, in percent.

cftc.name: max_rate
cftc.description: Highest executed rate at the node, in percent.

cftc.name: is_capped
cftc.description: Whether any trade at the node had its notional disseminated at the cap.

widget_config.name: OIS Policy Path
widget_config.description: Expected central-bank overnight-rate path, read from forward-starting OIS reported to the DTCC.

/cftc/fx_forward_points.description: Get FX forward points, built from executed forwards and FX swaps.
/cftc/fx_forward_points.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.fx_forward_points(provider='cftc')
# Get USDJPY forward points.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_points(pair='USDJPY', provider='cftc')
# Include sub-institutional trades, which price away from the market.
obb.cftc.fx_forward_points(pair='EURUSD', min_notional=0, provider='cftc')
```

cftc.name: pair
cftc.description: Currency pair, in market quoting convention. The USD/EM pairs (USDKRW, USDINR, USDBRL, ...) are non-deliverable forwards.

cftc.name: source
cftc.description: Where the trades come from. 'search' queries a window of dissemination days and prices each tenor from the most recent day it traded in depth. 'slice' uses a single day's cumulative file, which leaves thin tenors missing and yields nothing on a weekend.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC). With source='search' this ends the lookback window, and defaults to today. With source='slice' it selects one day's file, and defaults to the most recent published. History is retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: lookback_days
cftc.description: Number of dissemination days to search back over, ending on `date`. Only used when source='search'. A longer window fills in more tenors, at the cost of pricing the thin ones further from today; check `staleness_days`. The source caps a search at 180 days.

cftc.name: min_notional
cftc.description: Minimum trade notional, in the base currency. Sub-institutional prints trade percent away from the interbank market and would otherwise dominate a tenor's median. Set to 0 to keep every trade.

cftc.name: min_trades
cftc.description: Drop tenors priced by fewer than this many trades. The default keeps every tenor, because one executed trade is still a price; `num_trades`, `min_rate` and `max_rate` say how thin it is.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the source data locally. Closed dissemination days are immutable and are never re-fetched; daily files are revalidated against the source ETag.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Date of the curve, being that of its freshest tenor.

cftc.name: as_of_date
cftc.description: Dissemination date the tenor's trades were reported on.

cftc.name: staleness_days
cftc.description: Days between the tenor's as-of date and the curve's date. Zero on the freshest tenors.

cftc.name: pair
cftc.description: Currency pair, in market quoting convention.

cftc.name: tenor
cftc.description: Tenor bucket of the observation.

cftc.name: tenor_days
cftc.description: Lower bound of the tenor bucket, in days.

cftc.name: spot_rate
cftc.description: Spot rate of the tenor's as-of date, the median of that day's trades settling within two days, or of its shortest-dated tenor for a non-deliverable pair.

cftc.name: forward_rate
cftc.description: Median executed forward rate at the tenor.

cftc.name: forward_points
cftc.description: Executed forward rate less spot, in pips.

cftc.name: theoretical_points
cftc.description: Covered-interest-parity forward points from the two legs' rate curves, in pips - each leg's OIS, or its fixed-float IRS for an EM currency with no OIS. Present only when both legs have a curve; for a non-deliverable pair its gap to the executed points (`basis_points`) is the NDF basis to onshore rates.

cftc.name: basis_points
cftc.description: Executed points less the CIP points, in pips: positive where the market pays over covered-interest-parity fair value, negative under.

cftc.name: quotation
cftc.description: Whether the base is at a forward premium (executed points positive, forward above spot) or a discount (points negative, forward below spot).

cftc.name: carry
cftc.description: Whether a long base-currency forward position earns or pays the points to the forward date. It earns at a discount - the base out-yields the quote, so it is bought forward below spot - and pays at a premium. The short-base side is the opposite (Lehman Brothers, FX Training Manual: pay or earn the points).

cftc.name: num_trades
cftc.description: Number of executed trades aggregated into the tenor.

cftc.name: total_notional
cftc.description: Sum of the base currency notional of the tenor's trades.

cftc.name: min_rate
cftc.description: Lowest executed rate aggregated into the tenor. A wide gap to `max_rate` marks a dispersed bucket whose median may be off-market - read it alongside `num_trades` before relying on the point.

cftc.name: max_rate
cftc.description: Highest executed rate aggregated into the tenor. A wide gap to `min_rate` marks a dispersed bucket whose median may be off-market - read it alongside `num_trades` before relying on the point.

widget_config.name: FX Forward Points
widget_config.description: FX forward points built from executed forwards and FX swaps.

cftc.name: pair
cftc.description: Currency pair, in market quoting convention. Limited to the pairs whose options are reported to the CFTC in enough depth to build a surface each day. The USD/EM pairs (USDBRL, USDKRW, ...) are built from non-deliverable options against a spot and forward taken from the reported non-deliverable forwards.

cftc.name: basis
cftc.description: How the surface is built: 'empirical' medians the traded options at each grid strike (gaps where nothing traded); 'theoretical' fits a lognormal-SABR smile per expiry and evaluates it on the grid (smooth, gap-free).

cftc.name: date

cftc.name: min_trades

cftc.name: use_cache

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date of the options.

cftc.name: pair

cftc.name: strike
cftc.description: Strike price of the underlying, on a grid of offsets from spot.

cftc.name: strike_offset
cftc.description: The strike's distance from spot, positive above spot: in points for a deliverable major, in basis points of spot for a non-deliverable USD/EM pair.

cftc.name: vol_1w

cftc.name: vol_2w

cftc.name: vol_6m

cftc.name: vol_9m

cftc.name: vol_1y
cftc.description: 1-year implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

cftc.name: vol_2y
cftc.description: 2-year implied volatility at the strike, in percent (5.4 is 5.4%).

cftc.name: num_options
cftc.description: Number of options aggregated into the strike row, across expiries.

/cftc/fx_option_trades.description: Get the raw FX option transactions disseminated by DTCC, newest first.
/cftc/fx_option_trades.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.cftc.fx_option_trades(provider='cftc')
# Get the newly executed EURUSD option prints.
obb.cftc.fx_option_trades(pair='EURUSD', action_type='NEWT', provider='cftc')
# Get the non-deliverable option prints (BRL, KRW, INR, ...).
obb.cftc.fx_option_trades(option_type='Non-Deliverable', provider='cftc')
# Get the 20 largest JPY option prints of the day.
obb.cftc.fx_option_trades(pair='JPY', min_notional=50000000, limit=20, provider='cftc')
```

cftc.name: pair
cftc.description: Filter to a pair or currency, matched against the two reported legs. 'EURUSD', 'EUR/USD' and 'EUR USD' all match EUR/USD; a single code like 'JPY' matches every pair with that leg. Default is every pair, deliverable and non-deliverable.

cftc.name: option_type
cftc.description: Filter by option family: Vanilla, Non-Deliverable (cash-settled EM options), Digital, Barrier, or Target. Default is every family.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC). Default is the most recent day whose file holds option prints; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Files are retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: action_type
cftc.description: Filter by the action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). Default is every action; pass NEWT for newly executed trades only.

cftc.name: settlement_currency
cftc.description: Filter to options cash-settled in this currency, e.g. 'USD' for the USD-settled non-deliverable options. Deliverable options carry no settlement currency and are excluded by it. Default is every settlement.

cftc.name: min_notional
cftc.description: Drop prints whose larger notional leg is disseminated below this amount. The two legs value the same trade in each currency, so the larger is a currency-agnostic size proxy. Amounts above the reporting cap disseminate at the cap.

cftc.name: ticker
cftc.description: Filter to the exact UPI ticker, the Unique Product Identifier the source's TICKER report keys on. Default is every product. A ticker query is answered by the source's search API, cached per day, not the daily files.

cftc.name: limit
cftc.description: Number of prints to return, newest execution first. Default is all matching.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

cftc.name: event_timestamp
cftc.description: Date and time the reported event occurred, in UTC. The tape is ordered by it, newest first: a termination or correction of an old trade is dated when it is reported now, not when the trade was struck.

cftc.name: execution_timestamp
cftc.description: Date and time the option was originally executed, in UTC. It equals the reported time on a new trade, but predates it on an amendment or termination.

cftc.name: pair
cftc.description: Currency pair of the option, its two reported legs.

cftc.name: option_type
cftc.description: Option family, read from the FISN: Vanilla, Non-Deliverable (cash-settled, `settlement_currency` is the payout leg), Digital, Barrier, or Target. Derived, not disseminated.

cftc.name: action_type
cftc.description: Action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). An amendment carries the original trade's identifier in `original_trade_key`.

cftc.name: call_currency
cftc.description: Currency the option holder has the right to buy.

cftc.name: call_amount
cftc.description: Notional of the currency bought, in `call_currency`.

cftc.name: put_currency
cftc.description: Currency the option holder has the right to sell.

cftc.name: put_amount
cftc.description: Notional of the currency sold, in `put_currency`.

cftc.name: strike
cftc.description: Strike price of the option, oriented as `strike_pair` states.

cftc.name: strike_pair
cftc.description: Quotation the strike is expressed in, e.g. 'EUR/USD'. When absent, the strike follows `exchange_rate_basis`.

cftc.name: strike_notation
cftc.description: Format the strike is expressed in, per the CFTC Part 43/45 spec: 1 (a price, i.e. the exchange rate) or 3 (a decimal).

cftc.name: expiration_date
cftc.description: Date the option expires.

cftc.name: days_to_expiry
cftc.description: Calendar days from execution to expiration.

cftc.name: premium_amount
cftc.description: Option premium paid, in `premium_currency`.

cftc.name: premium_currency
cftc.description: Currency the premium is denominated in.

cftc.name: settlement_currency
cftc.description: Currency a cash-settled option pays out in. Populated for non-deliverable options, whose non-deliverable leg settles in this currency rather than delivering.

cftc.name: cleared
cftc.description: Whether the transaction is centrally cleared: Y (cleared), N (not cleared), or I (intent to clear).

cftc.name: venue
cftc.description: ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility, or BILT when the reporting counterparty could not determine the venue.

cftc.name: exchange_rate
cftc.description: Posted exchange rate on the trade, oriented as `exchange_rate_basis` states. A proxy for spot at execution, the pricing reference for the strike.

cftc.name: exchange_rate_basis
cftc.description: Quotation the exchange rate is expressed in, e.g. 'EUR/USD'.

cftc.name: notional_1
cftc.description: Leg 1 notional, in `notional_currency_1`.

cftc.name: notional_currency_1
cftc.description: Currency of the leg 1 notional.

cftc.name: notional_2
cftc.description: Leg 2 notional, in `notional_currency_2`.

cftc.name: notional_currency_2
cftc.description: Currency of the leg 2 notional.

cftc.name: effective_date
cftc.description: Date the option comes into effect.

cftc.name: first_exercise_date
cftc.description: First date the option may be exercised.

cftc.name: event_type
cftc.description: Reason for the action: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation), ETRM (early termination), EXER (exercise), or CLRG (clearing).

cftc.name: block_trade
cftc.description: Whether the print is reported as a block trade.

cftc.name: prime_brokerage
cftc.description: Whether the transaction is a prime-brokerage transaction.

cftc.name: package_trade
cftc.description: Whether the print is one leg of a package transaction - a strategy (straddle, risk reversal, calendar spread, ...) whose legs are negotiated and priced together.

cftc.name: package_id
cftc.description: Grouping key shared by the legs of one package - its execution time and package price or spread. Group on it to reassemble a strategy. Derived, not disseminated.

cftc.name: package_price
cftc.description: Price of the whole package, in the format `package_price_notation` states; the same on every leg. Present on price-quoted packages, where DTCC's 9.9999999999 not-provided placeholder has been dropped to null.

cftc.name: package_price_currency
cftc.description: Currency the package price is denominated in, when it is a monetary amount.

cftc.name: package_price_notation
cftc.description: Format of `package_price`: 1 (a monetary amount, in `package_price_currency`) or 3 (a decimal).

cftc.name: package_spread
cftc.description: Spread of the whole package; the same on every leg. Present on spread-quoted packages instead of a price.

cftc.name: package_spread_notation
cftc.description: Format of `package_spread`: 1 (a monetary amount) or 3 (a decimal).

cftc.name: upi_fisn
cftc.description: ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name, e.g. 'NA/O Van Call EUR USD'. Its Call/Put label is unreliable; use the call and put currencies.

cftc.name: underlier
cftc.description: UPI underlier name, the two legs of the pair as reported.

cftc.name: unique_product_identifier
cftc.description: ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier.

cftc.name: dissemination_date
cftc.description: Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in.

cftc.name: trade_key
cftc.description: Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'FX:4419821879000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

cftc.name: original_trade_key
cftc.description: For an action other than 'New', the qualified identifier of the original trade being amended, corrected or terminated. Match it against a `trade_key` to follow a trade's lifecycle.

cftc.name: is_capped
cftc.description: Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap.

widget_config.name: FX Option Trades
widget_config.description: The raw FX option transactions reported to the CFTC, newest first.

/cftc/fx_forward_trades.description: Get the raw FX forward and swap transactions disseminated by DTCC, newest first.


cftc.name: pair
cftc.description: Filter to a pair or currency, matched against the two reported legs. 'EURUSD', 'EUR/USD' and 'EUR USD' all match EUR/USD; a single code like 'INR' matches every pair with that leg. Default is every pair, deliverable and non-deliverable.

cftc.name: product_type
cftc.description: Filter by product: Forward (deliverable outright), Non-Deliverable Forward (cash-settled EM outright), FX Swap (near and far legs), Non-Deliverable Swap, or Non-Standard Forward. Default is every product.

cftc.name: date
cftc.description: Dissemination date (UTC). Default is the most recent day whose file holds forward prints; a file is published every calendar day, but weekends and holidays carry almost none. Files are retained for 366 days.

cftc.name: action_type
cftc.description: Filter by the action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). Default is every action; pass NEWT for newly executed trades only.

cftc.name: settlement_currency
cftc.description: Filter to trades whose leg-1 settlement currency matches, e.g. 'USD' for the USD-settled trades regardless of pair orientation. Non-deliverable forwards and swaps always carry it - their single cash-settlement currency; deliverable trades carry it only when reported. Default is every settlement.

cftc.name: min_notional
cftc.description: Drop prints whose larger notional leg is disseminated below this amount. The two legs value the same trade in each currency, so the larger is a currency-agnostic size proxy. Amounts above the reporting cap disseminate at the cap.

cftc.name: ticker
cftc.description: Filter to the exact UPI ticker, the Unique Product Identifier the source's TICKER report keys on. Default is every product. A ticker query is answered by the source's search API, cached per day, not the daily files.

cftc.name: limit
cftc.description: Number of prints to return, newest execution first. Default is all matching.

cftc.name: use_cache
cftc.description: Cache the daily file locally, revalidating it against the source ETag.

cftc.name: event_timestamp
cftc.description: Date and time the reported event occurred, in UTC. The tape is ordered by it, newest first: a termination or correction of an old trade is dated when it is reported now, not when the trade was struck.

cftc.name: execution_timestamp
cftc.description: Date and time the forward was originally executed, in UTC. It equals the reported time on a new trade, but predates it on an amendment or termination.

cftc.name: pair
cftc.description: Currency pair of the forward, its two reported legs.

cftc.name: product_type
cftc.description: Product, read from the FISN: Forward, Non-Deliverable Forward (`settlement_currency` is the cash-settled leg), FX Swap, Non-Deliverable Swap, or Non-Standard Forward. Derived, not disseminated.

cftc.name: action_type
cftc.description: Action reported: NEWT (new), MODI (modify), CORR (correct), TERM (terminate), EROR (error), or REVI (revive). An amendment carries the original trade's identifier in `original_trade_key`.

cftc.name: exchange_rate
cftc.description: Agreed forward rate on the trade, oriented as `exchange_rate_basis` states. For an FX swap it is the rate of the disseminated leg.

cftc.name: exchange_rate_basis
cftc.description: Quotation the forward rate is expressed in, e.g. 'USD/INR'.

cftc.name: notional_1
cftc.description: Leg 1 notional, in `notional_currency_1`.

cftc.name: notional_currency_1
cftc.description: Currency of the leg 1 notional.

cftc.name: notional_2
cftc.description: Leg 2 notional, in `notional_currency_2`.

cftc.name: notional_currency_2
cftc.description: Currency of the leg 2 notional.

cftc.name: settlement_currency
cftc.description: Settlement currency of leg 1. For a non-deliverable forward or swap it is the single currency the net cash settles in rather than delivering; a deliverable trade carries the physical settlement currency of leg 1 when reported.

cftc.name: effective_date
cftc.description: Date the forward comes into effect.

cftc.name: expiration_date
cftc.description: Date the forward settles.

cftc.name: days_to_expiry
cftc.description: Calendar days from execution to expiration.

cftc.name: cleared
cftc.description: Whether the transaction is centrally cleared: Y (cleared), N (not cleared), or I (intent to clear).

cftc.name: venue
cftc.description: ISO 10383 segment MIC of the trading facility, or BILT when the reporting counterparty could not determine the venue.

cftc.name: event_type
cftc.description: Reason for the action: TRAD (trade), NOVA (novation), ETRM (early termination), or CLRG (clearing).

cftc.name: block_trade
cftc.description: Whether the print is reported as a block trade.

cftc.name: prime_brokerage
cftc.description: Whether the transaction is a prime-brokerage transaction.

cftc.name: package_trade
cftc.description: Whether the print is one leg of a package transaction - legs negotiated and priced together, such as the near and far legs of a swap booked as a package.

cftc.name: package_id
cftc.description: Grouping key shared by the legs of one package - its execution time and package price or spread. Group on it to reassemble the package. Derived, not disseminated.

cftc.name: package_price
cftc.description: Price of the whole package, in the format `package_price_notation` states; the same on every leg. Present on price-quoted packages, where DTCC's 9.9999999999 not-provided placeholder has been dropped to null.

cftc.name: package_price_currency
cftc.description: Currency the package price is denominated in, when it is a monetary amount.

cftc.name: package_price_notation
cftc.description: Format of `package_price`: 1 (a monetary amount, in `package_price_currency`) or 3 (a decimal).

cftc.name: package_spread
cftc.description: Spread of the whole package; the same on every leg. Present on spread-quoted packages instead of a price.

cftc.name: package_spread_notation
cftc.description: Format of `package_spread`: 1 (a monetary amount) or 3 (a decimal).

cftc.name: upi_fisn
cftc.description: ISO 18774 Financial Instrument Short Name, e.g. 'NA/Fwd NDF INR USD'.

cftc.name: underlier
cftc.description: UPI underlier name, the two legs of the pair as reported.

cftc.name: unique_product_identifier
cftc.description: ISO 4914 Unique Product Identifier.

cftc.name: dissemination_date
cftc.description: Date the SDR publicly disseminated the print, being the report date of the file it was published in.

cftc.name: trade_key
cftc.description: Asset-class-qualified dissemination identifier, e.g. 'FX:4419882315000000101'. The qualifier keeps the 19-digit identifier out of IEEE-754 double range, which truncates it past its 16th digit.

cftc.name: original_trade_key
cftc.description: For an action other than 'New', the qualified identifier of the original trade being amended, corrected or terminated. Match it against a `trade_key` to follow a trade's lifecycle.

cftc.name: is_capped
cftc.description: Whether any amount on the print was disseminated at a reporting cap.

widget_config.name: FX Forward Trades
widget_config.description: The raw FX forward and swap transactions reported to the CFTC, newest first.

/famafrench/factors.description:
Fama-French factors.

Metadata for the selected dataset are returned in the
`extra['results_metadata']` field of the response.

Source
------

https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html

All returns are in U.S. dollars, include dividends and capital gains,
and are not continuously compounded.

Market is the return on a region's value-weight market portfolio
minus the U.S. one month T-bill rate.

The Fama/French 5 factors (2x3) are constructed using the 6,
value-weight, portfolios formed on size and book-to-market, the 6,
value-weight, portfolios formed on size and operating profitability,
and the 6, value-weight, portfolios formed on size and investment.

To construct the SMB, HML, RMW, and CMA factors, we sort stocks in a
region into two market cap and three respective book-to-market equity (B/M),
operating profitability (OP), and investment (INV) groups at the end of each June.

Big stocks are those in the top 90% of June market cap for the region,
and small stocks are those in the bottom 10%.
The B/M, OP, and INV breakpoints for a region are the 30th and 70th percentiles
of respective ratios for the big stocks of the region.

Rm–Rf for July of year t to June of t+1 include all stocks
for which we have market equity data for June of t.
SMB, HML, RMW, and CMA for July of year t to June of t+1 include all stocks
for which we have market equity data for December of t-1
and June of t, (positive) book equity data for t-1 (for SMB, HML, and RMW),
non-missing revenues and at least one of the following: cost of goods sold,
selling, general and administrative expenses, or interest expense for
t-1 (for SMB and RMW), and total assets data for t-2 and t-1 (for SMB and CMA).

The momentum and short term reversal portfolios are reconstituted monthly
and the other research portfolios are reconstituted annually.
We reconstruct the full history of returns each month when we update the portfolios.
/famafrench/factors.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Fama-French 3-factors data for America, default is monthly.
obb.famafrench.factors(provider='famafrench')
# Fama-French 5-factors data for Europe.
obb.famafrench.factors(provider='famafrench', region='europe', factor='5_factors')
```

famafrench.description: Region of focus. Default is America.

famafrench.name: frequency
famafrench.description: Frequency of the factor data.Not all are available for all regions, and intervals depend on the factor selected. Weekly is only available for the US 3-Factor Model.

famafrench.name: end_date

famafrench.name: mkt_rf
famafrench.description: Excess return on the market, value-weighted return of all firms, minus the one-month Treasury bill rate. Not returned for momentum or reversal factors.

famafrench.name: smb
famafrench.description: Small minus big (SMB) factor returns. Average return of small minus big stock portfolios. Not returned for momentum or reversal factors.

/famafrench/us_portfolio_returns.description:
US Portfolio returns.

Metadata for the selected dataset are returned in the
`extra['results_metadata']` field of the response.

Source
------

https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html

All returns are in U.S. dollars, include dividends (unless the portfolio is 'wout_div')
and capital gains, and are not continuously compounded.


The momentum and short term reversal portfolios are reconstituted monthly
and the other research portfolios are reconstituted annually.
We reconstruct the full history of returns each month when we update the portfolios.


Size and Book-to-Market Portfolios
----------------------------------

- Small Value
- Small Neutral
- Small Growth
- Big Value
- Big Neutral
- Big Growth

BE < 0; bottom 30%, middle 40%, top 30%; quintiles; deciles.
Firms with negative book equity are in only the BE < 0 portfolio.

Size and Operating Profitability Portfolios
-------------------------------------------

- Small Robust
- Small Neutral
- Small Weak
- Big Robust
- Big Neutral
- Big Weak

Operating Profitability bottom 30%, middle 40%, top 30%; quintiles; deciles.

Size and Investment Portfolios
------------------------------

- Small Conservative
- Small Neutral
- Small Aggressive
- Big Conservative
- Big Neutral
- Big Aggressive

ME < 0 (not used); bottom 30%, middle 40%, top 30%; quintiles; deciles.
Investment bottom 30%, middle 40%, top 30%; quintiles; deciles.

Definitions
-----------

ME : Market Equity

Market equity (size) is price times shares outstanding.
Price and shares outstanding are from CRSP.

BE : Book Equity

Book equity is constructed from Compustat data or collected from the
Moody’s Industrial, Financial, and Utilities manuals.
BE is the book value of stockholders’ equity, plus balance sheet deferred taxes
and investment tax credit (if available), minus the book value of preferred stock.
Depending on availability, we use the redemption, liquidation, or par value (in that order)
to estimate the book value of preferred stock. Stockholders’ equity is the value reported
by Moody’s or Compustat, if it is available. If not, we measure stockholders’ equity as
the book value of common equity plus the par value of preferred stock,
or the book value of assets minus total liabilities (in that order).

See Davis, Fama, and French, 2000,
“Characteristics, Covariances, and Average Returns: 1929-1997”
Journal of Finance, for more details.

BE/ME : Book-to-Market

The book-to-market ratio used to form portfolios in June of year t is book equity
for the fiscal year ending in calendar year t-1,
divided by market equity at the end of December of t-1.

OP : Operating Profitability

The operating profitability ratio used to form portfolios in June of year t is annual revenues
minus cost of goods sold, interest expense, and selling, general, and administrative expense
divided by the sum of book equity and minority interest for the last fiscal year ending in t-1.

INV : Investment

The investment ratio used to form portfolios in June of year t is the change in total assets
from the fiscal year ending in year t-2 to the fiscal year ending in t-1,
divided by t-2 total assets.

E/P : Earnings/Price

Earnings is total earnings before extraordinary items, from Compustat.
The earnings/price ratio used to form portfolios in June of year t is earnings
for the fiscal year ending in calendar year t-1,
divided by market equity at the end of December of t-1.

CF/P : Cashflow/Price

Cashflow is total earnings before extraordinary items, plus equity’s share of depreciation,
plus deferred taxes (if available), from Compustat. Equity’s share is defined as market equity
divided by assets minus book equity plus market equity.
The cashflow/price ratio used to form portfolios in June of year t is the cashflow for the
fiscal year ending in calendar year t-1, divided by market equity at the end of December of t-1.

D/P : Dividend Yield

The dividend yield used to form portfolios in June of year t is the total dividends paid
from July of t-1 to June of t per dollar of equity in June of t.
The dividend yield is computed using the with and without dividend returns from CRSP,
as described in Fama and French, 1988, “Dividend yields and expected stock returns,”
Journal of Financial Economics 25.

/famafrench/country_portfolio_returns.description:
Country portfolio returns.

Metadata for the selected dataset are returned in the
`extra['results_metadata']` field of the response.

Source
------

https://mba.tuck.dartmouth.edu/pages/faculty/ken.french/data_library.html

We form value and growth portfolios in each country using four valuation ratios:

- book-to-market (B/M)
- earnings-price (E/P)
- cash earnings to price (CE/P)
- dividend yield (D/P)

We form the portfolios at the end of December each year by sorting on one of the four ratios and
then compute value-weighted returns for the following 12 months.

The value portfolios (High) contain firms in the top 30% of a ratio
and the growth portfolios (Low) contain firms in the bottom 30%.

There are two sets of portfolios.

In one, firms are included only if we have data on all four ratios.

In the other, a firm is included in a sort variable's portfolios
if we have data for that variable.

The market return (Mkt) for the first set is the value weighted average of the returns
for only firms with all four ratios.

The market return for the second set includes all firms with book-to-market data,
and Firms is the number of firms with B/M data.

famafrench.name: breakpoint_type
famafrench.description:
Type of breakpoint to fetch.

The breakpoints for month t use all NYSE stocks that have a CRSP share code of 10 or 11
and have good shares and price data. We exclude closed end funds and REITs.

Breakpoints are computed either monthly or annually, see the description of each breakpoint type below.

Data contains every fifth percentile, from 5% to 100%.

ME
--

Market Equity. Market equity (size) is price times shares outstanding.
Price and shares outstanding are from CRSP.

ME breakpoints are computed for each month.
It is price times shares outstanding (divided by 1,000,000) at month end.

BE/ME
-----

BE/ME breakpoints are computed at the end of each June.
The BE used in June of year t is the book equity for the last fiscal year end in t-1.
ME is price times shares outstanding at the end of December of t-1.

The breakpoints for year t use all NYSE stocks for which we have ME for December of t-1
and (positive) BE for the last fiscal year end in t-1.

Operating Profitability
-----------------------

Operating Profitability breakpoints are computed at the end of each June.
OP for June of year t is annual revenues minus

- cost of goods sold
- interest expense
- selling, general, and administrative expenses

divided by book equity for the last fiscal year end in t-1.

Please be aware that some of the value-weight averages of operating profitability for deciles 1 and 10 are extreme.
These are driven by extraordinary values of OP for individual firms.
We have spot checked the accounting data that produce the extraordinary values
and all the numbers we examined accurately reflect the data in the firm's accounting statements.

The breakpoints for year t use all NYSE stocks for which we have (positive) book equity data for t-1,
non-missing revenues data for t-1, and non-missing data for at least one of the following:

- cost of goods sold
- selling, general and administrative expenses
- interest expense for t-1.

Investment
----------

Investment breakpoints are computed at the end of each June.
Inv used in June of year t is the change in total assets from the fiscal year ending in year t-2
to the fiscal year ending in t-1, divided by t-2 total assets.

The breakpoints for year t use all NYSE stocks for which we have total assets data for t-2 and t-1.

E/P
---

E/P (in percent) breakpoints are computed at the end of each June.
The E used in June of year t is the earnings for the last fiscal year end in t-1.
P (actually ME) is price times shares outstanding at the end of December of t-1.

The breakpoints for year t use all NYSE stocks for which we have ME for December of t-1
and (positive) earnings for the last fiscal year end in t-1.

CF/P
----

CF/P (in percent) breakpoints is computed at the end of each June.
The CF used in June of year t is the cash flow for the last fiscal year end in t-1.
P (actually ME) is price times shares outstanding at the end of December of t-1.

The breakpoints for year t use all NYSE stocks for which we have ME for December of t-1
and (positive) cash flow for the last fiscal year end in t-1.

D/P
---

D/P (in percent) breakpoints are computed at the end of each June.
The dividend yield in June of year t is the total dividends paid from July of t-1
to June of t per dollar of equity in June of t.

The breakpoints for year t use NYSE stocks for which we have at least
seven months (to compute the dividend yield) from July of t-1 to June of t.
(Only six monthly returns are required in June 1926.)
We do not include stocks that pay no dividends from July of t-1 to June of t.

Prior 2-12
----------

Prior return breakpoints are computed for each month.
The prior return at the end of month t is the cumulative return from month t-11 to month t-1.

The breakpoints for month t use NYSE stocks.
To be included, a stock must have a price for the end of month t-12 and a good return for t-1.
In addition, any missing returns from t-11 to t-2 must be -99.0, CRSP's code for a missing price.

standard.name: settlement_date
standard.description: The mid-month short interest report is based on short positions held by members on the settlement date of the 15th of each month. If the 15th falls on a weekend or another non-settlement date, the designated settlement date will be the previous business day on which transactions settled. The end-of-month short interest report is based on short positions held on the last business day of the month on which transactions settle. Once the short position reports are received, the short interest data is compiled for each equity security and provided for publication on the 7th business day after the reporting settlement date.

    ngl: Liquid or liquefied hydrocarbons recovered from gas separation plants and gas processing facilities.
    other_crude: Refinery feedstocks, additives/oxygenates, and other hydrocarbons.
    total_crude: The sum of the primary categories: crude oil + NGL + other.
    lpg: Liquefied petroleum gases, comprising propane and butane.
    naphtha: Naphtha used as feedstock for producing high octane gasoline and as feedstock for the chemical/petrochemical industries.
    gasoline: Motor gasoline and aviation gasoline; motor gasoline includes biogasoline, e.g. ethanol blends.
    kerosene: Kerosenes, comprising jet kerosene and other kerosene.
    jet_fuel: Kerosene type jet fuel: aviation fuel used for aviation turbine power units; a subset of the amount reported under kerosenes.
    gas_diesel_oil: Gas/diesel oil, for automotive and other purposes; biodiesel is included.
    fuel_oil: Heavy residual oil/boiler oil, including bunker oil.
    other_products: Refinery gas, ethane, petroleum coke, lubricants, white spirit and SBP, bitumen, paraffin waxes, and other petroleum products.
    total_products: The sum of all secondary product categories; demand for total products includes direct use of crude oil, NGL, and other hydrocarbons.

jodi.name: unit
jodi.description: The unit of measurement. kbd: thousand barrels per day; kbbl: thousand barrels; kl: thousand kilolitres; ktons: thousand metric tons; conversion_factor: barrels per thousand metric tons.

jodi.name: start_date
jodi.description: Start date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Defaults to the first data period, 2002-01-01.

jodi.name: end_date
jodi.description: End date of the data, in YYYY-MM-DD format.

jodi.name: use_cache
jodi.description: If True, the source tables are cached under the user cache directory and revalidated against the source at most once per day, downloading again only when JODI has published an update.

jodi.name: production
jodi.description: Production (primary products). Marketed production, after removal of impurities but including quantities consumed by the producer in the production process.

jodi.name: refinery_output
jodi.description: Refinery output (secondary products). Gross refinery output of finished products, including refinery fuel.

jodi.name: from_other_sources
jodi.description: From other sources (primary products). Inputs of additives, biofuels, and other hydrocarbons produced from non-oil sources such as coal, natural gas, and renewable energy.

jodi.name: receipts
jodi.description: Receipts (secondary products). Primary product receipts (quantities of oil used directly without processing in a refinery) plus recycled products. Receipts for other oil products include direct use of crude oil and NGL.

jodi.name: imports
jodi.description: Imports. Goods having physically crossed the international boundaries, excluding transit trade and international marine and aviation bunkers.

jodi.name: exports
jodi.description: Exports. Goods having physically crossed the international boundaries, excluding transit trade and international marine and aviation bunkers.

jodi.name: products_transferred
jodi.description: Products transferred. For primary products, the sum of products transferred and backflows from the petrochemical industry; for secondary products, imported petroleum products reclassified as feedstocks for further processing in the refinery, without delivery to final consumers.

jodi.name: interproduct_transfers
jodi.description: Interproduct transfers (secondary products). Reclassification of products because their specification has changed or because they are blended into another product; a negative entry indicates a product to be reclassified, a positive entry a reclassified product. Interproduct transfers for other oil products include interproduct transfers of crude oil and NGL.

jodi.name: direct_use
jodi.description: Direct use (primary products). Crude oil, NGL, and other hydrocarbons used directly without being processed in oil refineries, for example crude oil burned for electricity generation.

jodi.name: stock_change
jodi.description: Stock change. Closing minus opening stock level; a positive number corresponds to a stock build, a negative number to a stock draw.

jodi.name: statistical_difference
jodi.description: Statistical difference. Differences between observed supply flows and refinery intake or demand.

jodi.name: refinery_intake
jodi.description: Refinery intake (primary products). Observed refinery throughputs.

jodi.name: demand
jodi.description: Demand (secondary products). Deliveries or sales to the inland market (domestic consumption) plus refinery fuel plus international marine and aviation bunkers. Demand for other oil products includes direct use of crude oil, NGL, and other primary hydrocarbons.

jodi.name: closing_stocks
jodi.description: Closing stocks. The primary stock level at the end of the month within national territories; includes stocks held by importers, refiners, stock-holding organisations, and governments.

standard.description: The mid-month short interest report is based on short positions held by members on the settlement date of the 15th of each month. If the 15th falls on a weekend or another non-settlement date, the designated settlement date will be the previous business day on which transactions settled. The end-of-month short interest report is based on short positions held on the last business day of the month on which transactions settle. Once the short position reports are received, the short interest data is compiled for each equity security and provided for publication on the 7th business day after the reporting settlement date.

/oecd/presentation_table_choices.description:
Get presentation table choices for OECD data retrieval.

 Progressive cascading selector using the OECD metadata taxonomy.
 All data is discovered dynamically from the OECD SDMX metadata —
 topics, subtopics, dataflows, and their TABLE_IDENTIFIER dimension
 values are resolved at runtime.
/oecd/presentation_table_choices.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get the topic choices (step 0).
obb.oecd.presentation_table_choices()
# Get subtopic choices for the 'ECO' topic (step 1).
obb.oecd.presentation_table_choices(topic='ECO')
# Get table choices for topic and subtopic (step 2).
obb.oecd.presentation_table_choices(topic='ECO', subtopic='ECO.EO')
# Get country choices for a specific table (step 3).
obb.oecd.presentation_table_choices(topic='ECO', subtopic='ECO.EO', table='DF_QNA::T0101')
# Get frequency choices (step 4).
obb.oecd.presentation_table_choices(topic='ECO', subtopic='ECO.EO', table='DF_QNA::T0101', country='USA')
```

Aligns `data` and `factors_data` on their shared index, optionally subtracts a
risk-free column from the target, then runs an OLS regression of the target on
the factor columns (plus an intercept) for each named look-back period. Returns
one row per (`period`, `factor`) with the OLS coefficient, p-value, 95%
confidence interval, and the period's R-squared.

Designed to be paired with any factor provider; for Fama-French data, pipe the
`openbb-famafrench` provider's output into `factors_data`.

standard.name: data
standard.type: Data | DataFrame | Series | dict | list | list[DataFrame] | list[Data] | list[Series] | ndarray
standard.description: Target time series (index column plus the target column).

standard.name: factors_data
standard.description: Factor matrix (index column plus one column per factor).

standard.name: periods
standard.description: Named look-back periods to regress over, anchored to the latest factor observation. Supported values: '1 Month', '3 Month', 'YTD', '1 Year', '3 Year', 'Max'.

standard.name: target
standard.description: Name of the column in `data` to regress on the factor matrix.

standard.name: index

standard.name: risk_free_column
standard.description: Optional name of the risk-free rate column in `factors_data`. When provided, the target is regressed in excess form (target minus the risk-free column) and the column itself is dropped from the regressors.

standard.description: Whether to create a chart or not, by default False.

standard.name: period
standard.description: Look-back period the regression was run over.

standard.name: factor
standard.description: Factor name (or 'const' for the regression intercept).

standard.name: coefficient
standard.description: OLS coefficient estimate for the factor.

standard.name: p_value
standard.description: Two-sided p-value of the coefficient estimate.
