/usda/weather_bulletins.description:
Get current and historical weather bulletins with their PDF links.

This command returns only the results portion of the OBBject response.
It contains a list of dictionaries where each dictionary has 'label' and 'value' keys.
/usda/weather_bulletins.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get weather bulletins for the current year.
obb.usda.weather_bulletins(provider='usda')
# Get weather bulletins for May 2023, week 2.
obb.usda.weather_bulletins(provider='usda', year=2023, month=5, week=2)
# Get URLs for comparing versus 1 year ago and download the base64-encoded PDF content to memory.
from datetime import datetime
urls = []
for year in [datetime.now().year, datetime.now().year - 1]:
    urls.append(obb.usda.weather_bulletins(year=year, month=5, week=2)[0]['value'])
pdfs = obb.usda.weather_bulletins_download(urls=urls)
```

/ustreasury/bulletin.description: Get tables from the quarterly Treasury Bulletin - offerings, ownership distribution, currency and coin, foreign currency positions, the Exchange Stabilization Fund, and internal revenue receipts.
/ustreasury/bulletin.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
obb.ustreasury.bulletin(table='ofs2', provider='us_treasury')
# Get the distribution of federal securities by class of investors.
obb.ustreasury.bulletin(table='ofs1', provider='us_treasury')
# Get offerings of marketable securities other than regular weekly bills.
obb.ustreasury.bulletin(table='pdo2', start_date='2025-01-01', provider='us_treasury')
```

us_treasury.name: table
us_treasury.description: The Treasury Bulletin table to query. pdo1: auction results of regular weekly Treasury bills; pdo2: auction results of other marketable securities (CMBs, notes, bonds, TIPS, FRNs); ofs1: distribution of federal securities by class of investors and type of issues; ofs2: estimated ownership of U.S. Treasury securities; uscc1: currency and coin outstanding and in circulation; uscc2: currency in circulation by denomination; fcp1: weekly foreign currency positions of major market participants; fcp2: monthly foreign currency positions of major market participants; fcp3: quarterly foreign currency positions of large market participants; esf1: Exchange Stabilization Fund balances; esf2: Exchange Stabilization Fund statement of net cost; ffo5: internal revenue receipts by state; ffo6: Customs and Border Protection collections of duties, taxes, and fees by district and port.

/ustreasury/award.description: Drill into a federal award from USAspending - its summary, transactions, subawards, federal accounts, funding, or the orders placed against a vehicle.
/ustreasury/award.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Get the summary of an award by its usaspending.gov id.
obb.ustreasury.award(award_id='CONT_IDV_15F06724A0000314_1549', provider='us_treasury')
# Drill into the subawards of an award.
obb.ustreasury.award(award_id='CONT_IDV_15F06724A0000314_1549', section='subawards', provider='us_treasury')
# Get the orders placed against an indefinite delivery vehicle.
obb.ustreasury.award(award_id='CONT_IDV_15F06724A0000314_1549', section='idv_children', provider='us_treasury')
```

/ustreasury/spending_explorer.description: Explore all federal spending for a fiscal year, broken down by budget function, agency, federal account, program activity, object class, recipient, or award.
/ustreasury/spending_explorer.examples:
Examples
--------

```python
from openbb import obb
# Break all federal spending down by object class.
obb.ustreasury.spending_explorer(provider='us_treasury')
# Drill into the agencies acquiring assets.
obb.ustreasury.spending_explorer(explorer_type='agency', scope='object_class:30', provider='us_treasury')
# Drill into one agency's federal accounts for an object class.
obb.ustreasury.spending_explorer(explorer_type='federal_account', scope='agency:1173', object_class='30', provider='us_treasury')
```

us_treasury.name: explorer_type
us_treasury.description: Dimension to break the spending down by. Every dimension works on its own except 'program_activity', 'recipient', 'award', 'award_category', which are too large to enumerate government-wide and need a scoping filter. A scope on the dimension being broken down is ignored, since breaking down by a dimension means showing every one of its entries.

us_treasury.name: fiscal_year
us_treasury.description: Federal fiscal year. When None, the most recent year the source has published is used. Data begins in FY2017 Q2.

us_treasury.name: period
us_treasury.description: Federal fiscal period to report through. Amounts are cumulative from the start of the fiscal year, so 'Through March' covers October through March. 'latest' resolves to the most recent period the source has published, because a period that has not closed yet is rejected.

us_treasury.name: budget_function
us_treasury.description: Scope the breakdown to one budget function, by its code.

us_treasury.name: budget_subfunction
us_treasury.description: Scope the breakdown to one budget sub-function, by its code.

us_treasury.name: agency
us_treasury.description: Scope the breakdown to one agency, by the id returned for an 'agency' breakdown.

us_treasury.description: Scope the breakdown to one federal account, by the id returned for a 'federal_account' breakdown.

us_treasury.description: Scope the breakdown to one program activity, by its id.

us_treasury.description: Scope the breakdown to one object class, by its code, e.g. '30' for Acquisition of assets.

us_treasury.name: recipient
us_treasury.description: Scope the breakdown to one recipient, by its id.

us_treasury.description: Name of the breakdown entry.

from openbb import obb

obb.ustreasury.recipient_search(keyword='Lockheed Martin', provider='us_treasury')

us_treasury.name: keyword
